titulo_en: The first scene had already begun

titulo_es.@es: Past perfect: una acción anterior a otra del pasado
titulo_es.@en: Past perfect: one action before another of the past

texto.@es: **When Alex returned, the first scene had already begun** (cuando Alex regresó, la primera escena ya había empezado). **Had begun** marca lo que ocurrió antes; **returned** es el punto pasado de referencia.
texto.@en: **When Alex returned, the first scene had already begun** (when Alex returned, the first scene had already started). **Had begun** marks what happened before; **returned** is the last reference point.

titulo.@es: By the time, after y before
titulo.@en: By the time, after and before

texto.@es: **By the time + pasado simple** suele acompañarse de past perfect para destacar que algo ya se había completado: **By the time we arrived, the film had started.** **After** y **before** ya pueden dejar claro el orden, así que el pasado simple también es natural en secuencias sencillas: **After she left, he called.** El past perfect añade énfasis o destaca una acción anterior relevante.
texto.@en: **By the time + pasado simple** is usually accompanied by perfect past to highlight that something had already been completed: **By the time we arrived, the film had started.** **After** and **before** can already make the order clear, so the simple past is also natural in simple sequences: **After she left, he called.** The perfect past adds emphasis or highlights a relevant previous action.

titulo.@en: A late arrival at the theater

frases.es: La obra empezó a las siete.

frases.en: Alex arrived at the theatre at seven, but he had forgotten his ticket at home.
frases.es: Alex llegó al teatro a las siete, pero había olvidado la entrada en casa.

analisis.@en: She forgot before she got here.

frases.en: He went back home to get it.
By the time he returned, the first scene had already begun.
frases.es: Para cuando regresó, la primera escena ya había empezado.

frases.en: He found a seat before the interval and watched the rest of the performance.
frases.es: Encontró una butaca antes del descanso y vio el resto de la función.

pregunta.@es: What had Alex forgotten before he arrived at the theatre?
pregunta.@en: What had Alex forgotten before he arrived at the theater?

opciones.explicacion: The text says he had forgotten it at home.
The text does not mention a programme.

explicacion.@es: He arrived at seven; the forgotten item was his ticket.
explicacion.@en: He arrived at seven; the forbidden item was his ticket.

pregunta.@es: Which event happened before Alex returned to the theatre?
pregunta.@en: When event happened before Alex returned to the theatre?

opciones.explicacion: The text says it had already begun by the time he returned.

opciones.texto: He watched the rest of the play.
opciones.explicacion: He did this after finding his seat.
The text says he found a seat before the interval.

bloques.frase: By the time Alex returned, the first scene ___ already begun.

opciones.explicacion: Use **had + past participle** for the earlier past event.
This is present perfect, not past perfect.
This does not form the past perfect.

bloques.frase: By the time he returned, the first scene had already begun.

opciones.texto: Para cuando regresó, la primera escena ya había empezado.
opciones.explicacion: The scene began before his return.

opciones.texto: Cuando regresó, la primera escena empezó en ese momento.
opciones.explicacion: This says it began at the time he returned.

opciones.texto: Regresará cuando la primera escena haya empezado.
opciones.explicacion: This describes the future.

bloques.pregunta: Why did Alex go back home?

opciones.explicacion: The reading states that this was the reason.

opciones.texto: The play had not started yet.
opciones.explicacion: The play started at seven, and he arrived at seven.

opciones.explicacion: The text gives no such intention.

pregunta.@es: What does **had begun** show in “the first scene had already begun”?
pregunta.@en: What does **had begun** show in the first scene had already begun?

opciones.texto: The scene began before Alex returned.
opciones.explicacion: **Returned** is the later past reference point.

opciones.texto: The scene began after Alex returned.
opciones.explicacion: That reverses the order.
**Had begun** refers to the past.

bloques.frase: Alex had ___ his ticket at home.

explicacion.@es: This is the past simple form, not the participle used after **had**.
explicacion.@en: This is the past simple form, not the partition used after **had**.

opciones.explicacion: This is the base form.

pregunta.@es: Which sentence uses simple past for a single event at a stated past time?
pregunta.@en: When sentence uses simple past for a single event at a stated past time?

opciones.explicacion: A finished event at a specified past time normally takes past simple.

opciones.texto: The play had started at seven when Alex arrived.
opciones.explicacion: This marks the start as earlier than another past point.

opciones.texto: The play has started at seven.
opciones.explicacion: Present perfect does not normally go with a finished past time like **at seven**.

pregunta.@es: Which sentence presents events in a clear sequence without needing past perfect?
pregunta.@en: When sentence presents events in a clear sequence without needing past perfect?

opciones.texto: After she left, he called her.
opciones.explicacion: **After** already makes the order clear; simple past is natural.

opciones.texto: After she had left, he had called her.
opciones.explicacion: This is possible in some contexts, but the extra past perfect is not needed to show this simple order.

opciones.texto: After she leaves, he called her.

explicacion.@es: The tenses do not fit this past sequence.
explicacion.@en: The tends do not fit this past sequence.

intro.@es: **Past perfect = had + participio**. Sitúa una acción antes de otro momento pasado, sobre todo cuando esa relación importa o explica lo que ocurrió después. No hace falta usarlo en cada relato de hechos ordenados.
intro.@en: **Past perfect = had + participio**. It places an action before another time past, especially when that relationship matters or explains what happened next. There is no need to use it in every account of ordered facts.
